tip: Takes the dative: "işe geç kaldım", "derse geç kalma".

examples.en: Sorry, I'm late.
I was late for work because of traffic.
Hurry up, we'll be late for class.
Let me know if you're going to be late.

tip: "Eğilimli olmak" = to tend to.

examples.en: I tend to eat a lot when I'm stressed.

examples.tr: Gençler arasında yeni bir eğilim var.
examples.en: There's a new trend among young people.
Prices are tending to rise.
People tend to choose what they're used to.

tip: "Uykum var" = I'm sleepy. "Uykusuz" = sleepless.

examples.en: I'm very sleepy, I'm going to bed.
I didn't sleep last night.

examples.tr: İyi bir uyku her şeyi değiştirir.
examples.en: A good sleep changes everything.
Let me have a little nap in the afternoon.

tip: "Nasılsınız?" is polite or plural. A typical answer is "İyiyim, sen?"

examples.en: Hi, how are you?
"How are you?" "I'm good, thanks. You?"
We haven't seen each other for ages, how are you?
How is your mom? Say hi to her.

tip: "Amacım ... -mek" = My aim is to ...

examples.en: What is the purpose of this project?

examples.tr: Amacım bir yıl içinde akıcı konuşmak.
examples.en: My aim is to speak fluently within a year.
Our aim is customer satisfaction.
It's hard to live without a purpose.

tip: "Hata yapmak" = to make a mistake. "Benim hatam" = My fault.

examples.en: Sorry, my mistake.
Everyone makes mistakes.
I learned a lot from my mistakes.
An error occurred in the system.

tip: In casual speech people often say "he" or "hı hı" instead.

examples.en: Yes, I'd love to.
Yes, this is my bag.
"Are you ready?" "Yes, let's go."
Yes, you're right.

tip: Plural: "çocuklar". "Çocukluk" = childhood.

examples.en: How many children do you have?
The kids are playing in the park.
I was very naughty as a child.
I spent my childhood in this neighbourhood.

tip: Takes the ablative: "buradan uzak" = far from here.

examples.en: Is the airport far from here?
The school is very far from our house.
A distant relative of ours is coming tomorrow.
Hold the phone a bit further away.

meaning: to get off, to go down
tip: Takes the ablative: "otobüsten inmek". Also "aşağı inmek" = to go downstairs.

examples.en: I'll get off at the next stop.
I got out of the taxi and walked.

examples.tr: Aşağı iniyorum, bir şey ister misin?
examples.en: I'm going downstairs, do you want anything?
Prices have come down a bit.

tip: "Hiçbir fikrim yok" = I have no idea. "Fikrin ne?" = What's your opinion?

examples.en: What a great idea!
I have no idea.
What's your opinion on this?
I changed my mind, I'm not coming.

tip: "Esnek" = flexible. "Esnek çalışma" = flexible working.

examples.tr: Bu işin en güzel yanı esneklik.
examples.en: The best thing about this job is the flexibility.
We have flexible working hours.
There should be some flexibility in the plans.
My schedule is flexible, we'll arrange it to suit you.

tip: "Hazırlanmak" = to get ready (yourself).

examples.en: I'm making breakfast.
It took me two days to prepare the presentation.
Get ready, we're leaving in half an hour.
Have you packed your suitcase?

tip: "İzin verir misiniz?" = Would you allow me? / Excuse me, may I pass?

examples.en: Excuse me, may I get past?

examples.tr: Annem geç saatte dışarı çıkmama izin vermiyor.
examples.en: My mom doesn't let me go out late.

examples.tr: Burada fotoğraf çekmeye izin veriliyor mu?
examples.en: Is it allowed to take photos here?

examples.tr: Müdür bugün erken çıkmama izin verdi.
examples.en: The manager let me leave early today.

tip: "Çaba göstermek" = to make an effort.

examples.en: You made a lot of effort, well done.
With a little effort anything is possible.
This job requires a lot of effort.
Your efforts weren't in vain.

tip: "Kararlı" = determined.

examples.en: You succeeded thanks to your determination.
I'm very determined to quit smoking.
I admire her determination.
If you work with determination you'll reach your goal.

tip: Also used for driving and medicine: "araba kullanmak", "ilaç kullanmak".

examples.en: How do you use this app?
I've just learned to drive.

examples.tr: Günde iki kez bu ilacı kullanın.
examples.en: Use this medicine twice a day.
I try not to use plastic bags.

tip: "Şikayet etmek" = to complain. "Şikayetçi olmak" = to file a complaint.

examples.en: He's always complaining about the weather.
I made a complaint to customer service.
Do you have a complaint?
Instead of complaining, let's look for a solution.

tip: "Başka seçenek yok" = There's no other option.

examples.en: We have no other option.
Are there vegetarian options on the menu?
I'm torn between two options.
Let's consider all the options.

tip: Often paired with "de": "Belki de haklısın" - "Maybe you're right after all".

examples.en: Maybe I'll come tomorrow.
Maybe you're right.
Maybe we'll have a coffee.

examples.tr: Hava güzel olursa belki denize gideriz.
examples.en: If the weather's nice maybe we'll go to the sea.

tip: "Sakin ol" = calm down.

examples.en: Calm down, everything's fine.
The sea is very calm today.
We live in a quiet neighbourhood.
I try to stay calm in difficult situations.

tip: Use it to get a stranger's attention or to get past someone.

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the metro?
Excuse me, is this seat free?
Excuse me, can I get past?
Excuse me, what time is it?

tip: "Az kalsın" = almost. "En az" = at least.

examples.en: I'd like my tea with little sugar.
I almost missed the bus.

examples.tr: Günde en az sekiz saat uyumalısın.
examples.en: You should sleep at least eight hours a day.

examples.tr: Bu ay daha az para harcadım.
examples.en: I spent less money this month.

tip: "Kanıtlamak" = to prove.

examples.en: Is there any proof of this?
You need to prove what you're saying.
The police found new evidence.
Her success is proof of her hard work.

tip: "Erkek kardeş" = brother. "Kız kardeş" = sister. "Abla" = older sister, "abi" = older brother.

examples.en: How many siblings are there in your family?

examples.tr: Bir erkek kardeşim ve bir ablam var.
examples.en: I have a younger brother and an older sister.
My sibling and I share the same room.
My older brother is getting married this summer.

tip: Used to say something was already true: "Zaten biliyordum" = I already knew.

examples.en: I already knew.
We were already late anyway, so we didn't rush.
No need to come, I've already finished.
I was tired anyway, so I went to bed early.

tip: "Görüşüne göre" = in your view. "Görüşmek" = to meet up.

examples.en: What's your view on this?
We shared our views.
It's important to listen to different opinions.
I think his view is more reasonable.

tip: "Adresi bana at" = send me the address (casual).

examples.en: Could you text me your address?
I showed the address to the taxi driver.
This is my new address.
Is this address correct?

tip: "Yolda" = on the way. "Yolun açık olsun" = have a safe trip.

examples.en: I'm on my way, I'll be there in ten minutes.
Which road goes to the airport?
There's traffic because of roadworks.
There must be another way.

tip: "Öncelikle" = first of all.

examples.en: My priority right now is my health.
First of all, thank you all.
We need to set our priorities.
Priority is given to the elderly.

tip: Takes the dative for the destination: "bize gel", "eve geldim".

examples.en: Will you come over to ours tonight?
The bus has come, let's get on.
I came back from holiday yesterday.
A good idea came to my mind.

meaning: may it be easy (said to someone working)
tip: Say it to anyone working: a cashier, a colleague, a builder. Very polite and very Turkish.

examples.en: Hope work's going easy. Is there any bread left?
Walking into the office I said "kolay gelsin" to everyone.

examples.tr: Kolay gelsin, size bir şey soracaktım.
examples.en: Sorry to bother you while you work, I wanted to ask you something.
I hear you're moving, hope it goes smoothly!

tip: "Geç kalmak" = to be late. "Geç oldu" = it's got late.

examples.en: It's late, I should go home.
I went to bed late last night.
Better late than never.
The bus came late again.

tip: Used for warm, friendly people or places. "Samimi bir ortam" = a friendly atmosphere.

examples.tr: Çok samimi bir insan, hemen kaynaştık.
examples.en: She's a very warm person, we hit it off immediately.
The café has a friendly atmosphere.
We're not that close with him.
To be honest, I didn't really like it.

tip: Polite form: "yaşlı amca / yaşlı teyze". Opposite: "genç" (young).

examples.en: I gave my seat to an elderly lady.
My grandfather is old but very energetic.
It's important to show respect to the elderly.
Mostly elderly people have stayed in the village.

tip: The easiest way to give an opinion. "Sence?" asks for the other person's.

examples.en: I think this idea is very good.
In my opinion we should wait a bit.
Which one do you think is nicer?
I think it's going to rain tomorrow.

tip: Takes the dative: "sana inanıyorum". "İnanmıyorum!" = I can't believe it!

examples.en: I believe in you, you can do it.
I can't believe it, I passed the exam!
Don't believe what he says.
This is hard to believe.

tip: "Para kazanmak" = to earn money. "Maçı kazanmak" = to win the match.

examples.en: Our team won the match!
How much do you earn a month?
She won a prize in the competition.

examples.tr: Bu işten çok şey kazandım, özellikle deneyim.
examples.en: I gained a lot from this job, especially experience.

tip: For clothes: "Bunu deneyebilir miyim?" = Can I try this on?

examples.en: Can I try on this shirt?

examples.tr: Yeni bir tarif denedim, çok güzel oldu.
examples.en: I tried a new recipe, it turned out great.
Try once more, you can do it.
Have you ever tried Turkish coffee?

tip: "Unutma!" = Don't forget!

examples.en: I forgot my keys at home.
Don't forget the meeting, it's at three.
I forgot her birthday.
I will never forget this day.

tip: "dizi izlemek" = to watch a series. "Seyretmek" is a synonym.

examples.en: Shall we watch a film tonight?
We watched the match with friends.
Have you watched this series?
It feels like someone is watching us.

tip: Turkish breakfast is a big deal. "Kahvaltı yapmak" = to have breakfast.

examples.en: Let's have breakfast together on Sunday.
What would you like to eat for breakfast?
A spread breakfast is always very generous.
I left today without having breakfast.

tip: More formal than "sebep". Common in work and official contexts.

examples.en: Could you explain the reasoning behind the decision?

examples.tr: Geç kalmak için geçerli bir gerekçen yok.
examples.en: You have no valid excuse for being late.
The reason for the application's rejection wasn't given.
We should present each proposal with its justification.

tip: For telling stories or explaining: "Bana her şeyi anlat."

examples.en: Tell me about your holiday, how was it?
The teacher explained the topic very well.
Tell me everything from the beginning.
I can't explain what I mean.

tip: "Rüya görmek" = to dream. "Hayal" = dream in the sense of a wish.

examples.tr: Dün gece çok garip bir rüya gördüm.
examples.en: I had a very strange dream last night.
Sweet dreams!
It was like a day from a dream.

examples.tr: Hayalim bir gün kendi kafemi açmak.
examples.en: My dream is to open my own café one day.

tip: "Doğum günün kutlu olsun!" = Happy birthday!

examples.en: Happy birthday!
When is your birthday?
You're invited to the birthday party.
You didn't forget my birthday!

tip: "Zorunda olmak" = to have to: "gitmek zorundayım".

examples.tr: Türkçe zor ama çok güzel bir dil.
examples.en: Turkish is hard but a very beautiful language.
This question is very hard to solve.

examples.tr: Sabah erken kalkmak benim için zor.
examples.en: Getting up early is hard for me.
I have to leave early today.

tip: "Çözmek" = to solve.

examples.en: We must find a solution to this problem.
Every problem has a solution.
She suggested a practical solution.
It took me an hour to solve the puzzle.

tip: Pairs with the conditional: "Keşke gelseydin" - "I wish you had come".

examples.en: I wish you had come too.
I wish I had more time.
If only I had stayed home that day.

examples.tr: Keşke Türkçeyi daha önce öğrenmeye başlasaydım.
examples.en: I wish I had started learning Turkish earlier.

tip: "Ağlama" = don't cry.

examples.tr: Film o kadar duygusaldı ki ağladım.
examples.en: The film was so emotional that I cried.
The baby cried all night.
Don't cry, everything will be alright.
She cried with joy.

tip: "Varsaymak" = to assume. "Diyelim ki" is a casual "let's assume".

examples.tr: Bu sadece bir varsayım, kesin değil.
examples.en: This is just an assumption, it's not certain.
Don't make decisions based on wrong assumptions.

examples.tr: Diyelim ki yarın yağmur yağdı, ne yaparız?
examples.en: Let's say it rains tomorrow, what do we do?
I assumed everyone knew.

tip: "Susadım" = I'm thirsty. For hunger: "acıktım".

examples.en: I'm very thirsty, is there any water?
I got very thirsty after running.
If you're thirsty there's juice in the fridge.
I get thirsty quickly in the heat.

tip: Also for weather: "Hava kapalı" = It's overcast.

examples.en: The bank is closed today.
It's cloudy, it might rain.
The shop is closed at lunchtime.
Where is the indoor car park?

tip: "Buldum!" = Found it! Also "to think/find something": "Bu filmi sıkıcı buldum."

examples.en: I can't find my keys.
We finally found a good house.
I found this book very interesting.
We need to find a solution.

tip: "Gençler" = young people. "Gençlik" = youth.

examples.en: You look young, how old are you?

examples.tr: Şirketimizde çok genç bir ekip var.
examples.en: Our company has a very young team.
I travelled a lot when I was young.

examples.tr: Bu kafe gençler arasında çok popüler.
examples.en: This café is very popular among young people.

tip: "Kelime kelime" = word by word. "Sözcük" is a synonym.

examples.en: I learned a new word today.
What does this word mean?
I repeat the words out loud.
How do you pronounce this word?

tip: "Temizlik yapmak" = to do the cleaning.

examples.en: I cleaned the house at the weekend.
Could you wipe the table?
Cleaning the kitchen is always left to me.
Have you cleaned your room?

tip: "Düz gidin" = go straight on. Also "düz su" = still water.

examples.en: Go straight, then turn right.
A bottle of still water, please.
Her hair is very straight.
I'm looking for a plain white t-shirt.

tip: "İtiraz etmek" = to object. "İtirazım yok" = I have no objection.

examples.tr: Bu plana itirazı olan var mı?
examples.en: Does anyone object to this plan?
I have no objection, let's do it that way.
I appealed against the decision.
She accepted without any objection.

tip: "Akşam yemeği" = dinner. "Akşamları" = in the evenings.

examples.en: What are you doing this evening?
What shall we make for dinner?
I go for a walk in the evenings.
I'm at the office until the evening.

tip: The person helped takes the dative: "sana yardım edeyim".

examples.en: Could you help me?
Shall I help you?

examples.tr: Taşınırken arkadaşlarım bana çok yardım etti.
examples.en: My friends helped me a lot when I moved.
Thanks for helping.

tip: "İhtiyacım var" = I need. "Gerek" is similar but more casual.

examples.en: Do you need help?
I need some rest.
Let me know if you need anything.
Prices of basic necessities have gone up.

tip: "Acıktım" = I'm hungry. "Aç" is the adjective.

examples.en: I'm hungry, let's eat something.
I didn't get hungry at all until noon.
Are you hungry? The food is ready.
I get really hungry after exercise.

tip: Used for both liking and loving. "Seni seviyorum" = I love you.

examples.en: I like my coffee with milk.
I love you very much.
I don't like winter at all.
We really like our new neighbours.

tip: "Kendimi iyi hissediyorum" = I feel good.

examples.en: I feel really good today.
I feel a bit sick.
I understand how you feel.
I feel at home here.

tip: Receiver takes the dative: "bana ver". Also in many phrases: karar vermek, cevap vermek, ara vermek.

examples.en: Could you pass the salt?

examples.tr: Kardeşime doğum günü için bir kitap verdim.
examples.en: I gave my sibling a book for their birthday.
Give me a little time.
Let's take a five-minute break.

tip: "Sıkılmak" = to get bored. "Sıkıldım" = I'm bored.

examples.en: The film was very boring, we left halfway through.
Meetings are sometimes very boring.
I'm bored of sitting at home.

examples.tr: Hiç sıkıcı biri değil, çok eğlencelidir.
examples.en: He's not boring at all, he's a lot of fun.

tip: "Yemekten sonra" = after the meal. "Sonra görüşürüz" = see you later.

examples.en: Let's talk later.
Let's go for a walk after the meal.
I go to the gym after work.
Do your homework first, then play.

tip: "Yeter" = that's enough. "Yeterince" = enough (adverb).

examples.tr: Bu kadar yemek herkes için yeterli mi?
examples.en: Is this much food enough for everyone?
I didn't sleep enough.

examples.tr: Bu maaş geçinmek için yeterli değil.
examples.en: This salary isn't enough to live on.
That's enough, let's not talk anymore.

tip: "İşe gitmek" = to go to work. "İş yeri" = workplace. "İşim var" = I have something to do.

examples.en: I start work at nine.
I found a new job!
I have a lot to do today.
How's work going?

tip: "Ev arkadaşı" = flatmate. "İş arkadaşı" = colleague.

examples.en: He is my best friend.
I went out to lunch with my colleagues.
My flatmate is very tidy.
I want to make new friends.

tip: Synonym: "hep". "Her zamanki gibi" = as usual.

examples.en: I'm always by your side.
He was late as usual.
I always drink my coffee without sugar.
I always come to this café.

tip: Add a time to be specific: "yarın görüşürüz", "sonra görüşürüz".

examples.en: See you tomorrow!
Right, see you, take care of yourself.
See you at the meeting.
See you later, I need to leave now.

tip: Also used for smoking: "sigara içmek". "Çay içelim" = let's have tea.

examples.en: Shall we have a tea?

examples.tr: Günde en az iki litre su içmelisin.
examples.en: You should drink at least two litres of water a day.
I can't sleep after drinking coffee.
Take the medicine after meals.

tip: "Önlem almak" = to take precautions.

examples.en: We took precautions against winter.
Security measures have been increased.
Prevention is easier than cure.
Take the necessary precautions so you don't get sick.

tip: Strong agreement on its own, or strong negation with a negative verb.

examples.en: You're absolutely right.
You should definitely watch this film.
I definitely won't be late.
"Are you coming?" "Absolutely!"

tip: "Solda" = on the left. "Sola dön" = turn left.

examples.en: The supermarket is on the left, right on the corner.
Turn left at the second street.
My left foot hurts.
Who is the man standing on your left?

tip: "Yeni yılınız kutlu olsun" = Happy new year.

examples.en: I bought a new phone.
I'm new in this city.
I learned something new today.
When are you coming to our new house?

tip: Positive: "Artık hazırım" (I'm ready now). Negative: "artık gelmiyor" (doesn't come anymore).

examples.en: I need to go now.
I don't smoke anymore.
I can watch Turkish films now.
That's enough now!

tip: "Farkında olmak" = to be aware.

examples.en: Awareness of environmental issues is growing.
I'm aware of my mistake.

examples.tr: Bu kampanya farkındalık yaratmak için yapıldı.
examples.en: This campaign was run to raise awareness.
I didn't realise how tired I was.

tip: Also for a phone line: "Hat meşgul" = The line is busy. "Yoğun" is a common synonym.

examples.en: I'm very busy this week.
I called but the line was busy.
If you're busy, let's talk later.

examples.tr: Müdür şu an meşgul, bekleyebilir misiniz?
examples.en: The manager is busy right now, can you wait?

tip: "Yorum yapmak" = to comment. "Yorumlamak" = to interpret.

examples.en: She left a nice comment on my photo.
Have you read the restaurant's reviews?
I don't want to comment on this.
Everyone interprets this event differently.

tip: "Seni eve götüreyim" = Let me take you home.

examples.en: I'll take you to the airport.
I took the kids to school.
I need to take this to the post office.
Can you wrap the food? I'll take it away.

tip: Both the verb "to eat" and the noun "food". "Yemek yemek" = to eat a meal.

examples.en: What shall we eat at lunch?
Dinner is ready.
I haven't eaten anything today.
I love Turkish food.

tip: "Sonuç olarak" = in conclusion, as a result.

examples.en: Have the exam results been announced?
In the end everyone was satisfied.
My test results came back normal.
We got the result of our efforts.

tip: "Uzlaşmak" = to reach a compromise.

examples.en: We finally reached a compromise.
Compromise is essential in relationships.
The two sides couldn't reach an agreement.
If you're a bit more willing to compromise, the problem will be solved.

tip: Said when praising something good, especially children or someone's success, to ward off envy.

examples.en: Wow, bless him, how much the child has grown!
Wow, your Turkish is very good.
Your new house is lovely, bless it.
Wonderful, things are going well.

tip: "Şanslı" = lucky. "Şansına" = as luck would have it.

examples.en: Luck was on my side today.
How lucky you are!
Give it one more chance.

examples.tr: Şans eseri eski bir arkadaşıma rastladım.
examples.en: By chance I bumped into an old friend.

tip: "Tatile gitmek/çıkmak" = to go on holiday.

examples.en: Where are you going on holiday this summer?
I rested a lot on holiday.
Tomorrow is a public holiday, the banks are closed.
How was your holiday?

tip: For trips. "Yolun açık olsun" is a warmer alternative.

examples.en: Have a good trip, let me know when you arrive.
At the airport she wished us a good trip.
Safe travels, have a good trip!
Have a good trip, take care.

tip: The standard reply to an apology. "Sorun değil" means the same.

examples.en: "Sorry." "It's nothing."
It's no big deal, everyone makes mistakes.

examples.tr: Geç kalman önemli değil, gel yeter.
examples.en: It doesn't matter if you're late, just come.
No problem, we'll do it another time.

tip: Also light colours: "açık mavi". "Açık konuşmak" = to speak frankly.

examples.en: Is the supermarket open on Sunday?
I'm looking for a light blue shirt.
Let me be frank, I didn't like this idea.
Don't leave the window open.

tip: "Bayramınız kutlu olsun" = Happy holidays. Big ones: Ramazan Bayramı, Kurban Bayramı.

examples.en: Happy holidays!
At bayram we kiss the hands of our elders.
We're going to our hometown for the bayram holiday.
Children get pocket money at bayram.

tip: "Tehlike" = danger.

examples.en: It's dangerous to swim here.

examples.tr: Gece bu sokakta yürümek tehlikeli mi?
examples.en: Is it dangerous to walk on this street at night?
Driving fast is very dangerous.

examples.tr: Tehlikeli bir şey yok, merak etme.
examples.en: There's nothing dangerous, don't worry.

tip: "Yeni eve taşınmak" = to move into a new home.

examples.tr: Geçen ay yeni bir eve taşındık.
examples.en: We moved to a new house last month.
I'm thinking of moving to Izmir.
Moving house is very tiring.
When are you moving?

tip: "Başarılar!" = Good luck! / All the best! "Başarılı" = successful.

examples.en: I wish you success!
The secret of success is working consistently.
You gave a very successful presentation.
This success belongs to all of us.

meaning: to know (a person or place), to recognise
tip: "Bilmek" is for facts, "tanımak" for people and places.

examples.en: I've known her for years.
You've had a haircut, I didn't recognise you.
I don't know this city well.
Do you recognise me?

tip: Used for sympathy. "Çok yazık" means "such a shame".

examples.en: What a pity, the film has already started.
The cat got caught in the rain, poor thing.

examples.tr: Bu kadar yemeği atmak yazık olur.
examples.en: It would be a shame to throw away this much food.
It's a shame, we missed the ticket.

meaning: to get up, to stand up, to depart
tip: Also for transport leaving: "Tren saat üçte kalkıyor."

examples.en: I get up at seven every morning.
The train departs at nine.

examples.tr: Yaşlı bir teyzeye yer vermek için kalktım.
examples.en: I stood up to give my seat to an old lady.
Get up, we're going to be late!

tip: Used to accept something, or to start a new question: "Peki, sen?"

examples.en: Well then, what do you think?
Alright, we'll talk tomorrow.
And how much is this?
"I can't come." "Alright, no problem."

tip: "Kirli çamaşır" = dirty laundry.

examples.en: Put the dirty dishes in the dishwasher.
Your shoes have got very dirty.
The dirty laundry is in the basket.
This side of the sea is a bit dirty.

tip: "Sinirli" = angry, irritable. "Sinirlenme" = don't get angry.

examples.en: I got really angry in traffic.
Don't get angry, it was an accident.
My boss got angry when I was late.
I try not to get angry about little things.

meaning: to leave, to drop off, to quit
tip: "Sigarayı bırakmak" = to quit smoking. "Beni burada bırak" = drop me here.

examples.en: Can you drop me at the corner?
I left the key on the table.
I quit smoking last year.
Leave it, I'll do it.

tip: "İndirimde" = on sale. "İndirim yapmak" = to give a discount.

examples.en: Is this item on sale?
Is there a student discount?
I'm waiting for the November sales.
I'll give you a discount if you pay cash.

tip: Also "to be left": "Ekmek kalmadı" = There's no bread left.

examples.en: I'll stay at home tonight.
We stayed three nights at the hotel.
Is there any milk left?
I almost missed the bus.

tip: "Biraz daha" = a bit more. "Biraz sonra" = a bit later.

examples.en: I speak a little Turkish.
Would you like a bit more tea?
I'm leaving a bit later.
I'm a bit tired.

tip: "Telefon etmek" = to phone. "Telefonu açmak" = to answer.

examples.en: My phone battery is about to die.
I'll phone you in the evening.
Can I have your phone number?
I try not to look at my phone during meals.

tip: "Evde" = at home. "Eve" = (to) home. "Evden" = from home.

examples.en: I'm working from home today.
I'll call you when I get home.
Our new house is very close to the sea.
Make yourself at home.

meaning: get well soon / sorry that happened
tip: Said for illness, accidents or any bad experience that has happened.

examples.en: I heard you were sick, get well soon.
Your car broke down? Sorry to hear that.

examples.tr: Ameliyat iyi geçti, herkese geçmiş olsun.
examples.en: The surgery went well, wishing everyone the best.

examples.tr: Geçmiş olsun, bir şeye ihtiyacın olursa ara.
examples.en: Get well soon, call me if you need anything.

tip: "Bu süreçte" = during this process/period.

examples.en: How long does the visa process take?

examples.tr: Bu süreçte bana çok destek oldun.
examples.en: You supported me a lot during this time.
The learning process is different for everyone.
Can we speed up the process a bit?

tip: "Koşu" = a run.

examples.en: I ran to catch the bus.
She runs in the park every morning.
Don't run, the floor is wet!
I started running three days a week.

tip: Useful when learning words: meaning depends on "bağlam".

examples.en: The word's meaning changes depending on the context.
Don't take this sentence out of context.
It's hard to comment without knowing the context.

examples.tr: Bu bağlamda ne demek istediğini anladım.
examples.en: In this context I understood what you meant.

tip: "İade etmek" = to return (an item).

examples.en: I'd like to return this item.
The return period is fourteen days.
How long does the refund take?
Returns aren't accepted for items without a receipt.

tip: "Sağlık olsun" = never mind (as long as we're healthy). "Sağlıklı" = healthy.

examples.en: Health is more important than anything.
The phone broke, but never mind, what matters is we're well.
I'm trying to eat healthily.
Do you have health insurance?

tip: Use it to hurry someone or suggest doing something together: "Hadi gidelim."

examples.en: Come on, we're getting late!
Let's have a coffee.
Oh come on, try it once.
Right then, see you!

tip: "Doğru!" = That's right! Also "towards": "eve doğru" = towards home.

examples.en: Your answer is correct.
You're telling the truth.
This road goes towards the centre.
Did I hear right, are you moving?

tip: "Kiracı" = tenant. "Ev sahibi" = landlord.

examples.en: How much is the rent per month?
The landlord raised the rent.
I pay the rent on the fifth of every month.
We're renting, we haven't bought a house yet.

tip: Said for a new home, car, job or business, wishing that it brings good.

examples.en: Congratulations on your new home!
You bought the car, enjoy it!
Congratulations on your new job, all the best.
Congratulations on your shop, may business be good.

tip: Bread is at every Turkish meal. "Taze ekmek" = fresh bread.

examples.en: I bought fresh bread from the bakery.
One loaf of bread, please.
We're out of bread, could you buy some?
In Turkey bread is eaten with every meal.

tip: "Hediye etmek" = to give as a present.

examples.tr: Doğum günü için ne hediye alsam?
examples.en: What should I buy for a birthday present?

examples.tr: Bu kitabı sana hediye olarak aldım.
examples.en: I bought this book for you as a present.
Could you gift-wrap it?

examples.tr: En güzel hediye birlikte geçirilen zaman.
examples.en: The best gift is time spent together.

tip: Takes the dative: "işe başlamak", "Türkçe öğrenmeye başladım".

examples.en: The film starts at eight.
I'm starting my new job on Monday.
I started learning Turkish last year.
Come on, let's start!

meaning: never, not at all / ever (in questions)
tip: With a negative verb it means "never/at all". In questions it means "ever": "Hiç gittin mi?"

examples.en: Have you ever been to Istanbul?
I've never seen him.
I have no money left at all.
Not bad at all!

tip: One of the most used verbs. Many phrases: kahvaltı yapmak, spor yapmak, alışveriş yapmak.

examples.en: What are you doing tonight?
My mom made a great cake.
I like doing sport in the mornings.

examples.tr: Merak etme, ben hallederim, sen bir şey yapma.
examples.en: Don't worry, I'll handle it, you don't do anything.

tip: "Çok yorgunum" = I'm very tired. The verb is "yorulmak".

examples.en: I'm very tired today, I'll go to bed early.
You look tired, are you okay?

examples.tr: Uzun bir yolculuktan sonra yorgun ama mutluyduk.
examples.en: After a long journey we were tired but happy.
I try not to make decisions when I'm tired.

tip: Goes near the start of the sentence.

examples.en: Sometimes I walk to work.
Sometimes I don't want to do anything.
Sometimes we go to my parents' at the weekend.
It's normal to make mistakes sometimes.

tip: "İlerlemek" = to progress, to move forward.

examples.en: Your Turkish has made great progress!

examples.tr: Proje yavaş ama emin adımlarla ilerliyor.
examples.en: The project is progressing slowly but surely.
I note my progress every week.
Go on a bit further and you'll see it on the right.

tip: "Çok lezzetliydi, eline sağlık!" is the perfect compliment to a cook.

examples.en: This soup is very delicious.

examples.tr: Dün gittiğimiz restoranın yemekleri çok lezzetliydi.
examples.en: The food at the restaurant we went to yesterday was delicious.

examples.tr: Lezzetli ve sağlıklı bir tarif arıyorum.
examples.en: I'm looking for a tasty and healthy recipe.
It was delicious, thank you for cooking!

tip: "Ucuza almak" = to buy cheaply.

examples.en: The vegetables are very cheap at this market.
I got this jacket cheap in the sale.
We're looking for a cheap hotel.
Cheap meat makes a bland stew. (You get what you pay for.)

tip: "... hakkında düşünmek" = to think about. "Ne düşünüyorsun?" = What do you think?

examples.en: What do you think?
I need to think about this a bit.
I was thinking about you, are you okay?
We're thinking of moving.

tip: Said to someone who has lost a loved one. The reply is "dostlar sağ olsun".

examples.tr: Babanı kaybettiğini duydum, başın sağ olsun.
examples.en: I heard you lost your father, my condolences.
My condolences, I'm very sorry.
"My condolences." "Thank you, and long life to friends."
At the funeral I offered my condolences to everyone.

tip: "Rahatsız etmiyorum ya?" = I'm not disturbing you, am I?

examples.en: Sorry to bother you.
The noise is disturbing the neighbours.
Please do not disturb.
I'm not bothering you, am I?

tip: "Yavaş yavaş" = little by little, slowly.

examples.en: Please speak more slowly.
Traffic is very slow today.
Little by little my Turkish is improving.
Slow down, don't rush.

tip: Also a question: "Tamam mı?" means "Okay?" or "Deal?".

examples.en: Okay, let's meet at five.
I'll call tomorrow, okay?
Okay, I understand.
Everything's ready, we can go.

tip: "Bir sonraki durak" = the next stop.

examples.en: How many stops until I get off?
I'm getting off at the next stop.
I waited at the stop for twenty minutes.
The taxi rank is right on the corner.

tip: "İşbirliği yapmak" = to collaborate.

examples.en: Thank you for your cooperation.

examples.tr: İki şirket işbirliği yapmaya karar verdi.
examples.en: The two companies decided to collaborate.

examples.tr: Bu proje ancak işbirliğiyle başarılı olur.
examples.en: This project can only succeed through collaboration.
We teamed up with the neighbours and cleaned the street.

tip: "Şarj aleti" = charger. "Şarj etmek" = to charge.

examples.en: Do you have a charger?
I need to charge my phone.
My battery has dropped to five percent.

examples.tr: Bu kafede şarj edebileceğim bir priz var mı?
examples.en: Is there a socket in this café where I can charge?

tip: "Kolay gelsin" comes from this word.

examples.en: This recipe is very easy.
It wasn't as easy as I thought.

examples.tr: Oraya gitmek kolay, metroyla on dakika.
examples.en: It's easy to get there, ten minutes by metro.

examples.tr: Kolay bir iş değil ama yapabiliriz.
examples.en: It's not an easy job but we can do it.

tip: "Gerek" = need: "Gerek yok" = No need.

examples.en: What documents are needed for the application?
No need, I'll handle it.

examples.tr: Bu kadar para harcamak gerekli miydi?
examples.en: Was it necessary to spend this much money?
Call me if necessary.

tip: "Haber vermek" = to let someone know. "Haberin var mı?" = Did you hear?

examples.en: Let me know when you arrive.
I have good news!
Did you watch the evening news?
I had no idea about this.

tip: "Götürmek" is the opposite direction: to take something away.

examples.en: Could you bring bread on your way?
The waiter brought the menu.
What shall I bring to the party?
I'll bring your book tomorrow.

tip: "Genelde" is shorter and very common in speech.

examples.en: I usually get up at seven in the morning.
I'm usually at home at the weekend.

examples.tr: Kahvaltıda genellikle peynir ve zeytin yerim.
examples.en: I usually eat cheese and olives at breakfast.
He is usually a very calm person.

tip: Takes the accusative: "Onun adını hatırlamıyorum." "Hatırlatmak" = to remind.

examples.en: I don't remember his name.
Could you remind me tomorrow?
I always remember my childhood fondly.

examples.tr: Beni hatırladın mı? Geçen yıl tanışmıştık.
examples.en: Do you remember me? We met last year.

tip: "Sabahları" = in the mornings (habitually).

examples.en: We set off early in the morning.
I drink coffee in the mornings.
I'll call you tomorrow morning.
The weather was lovely this morning.

tip: "Takip etmek" = to follow. "Kargo takip" = parcel tracking.

examples.en: Can I track my parcel?
I follow you on social media.

examples.tr: Bu konuyu takip edip sana dönerim.
examples.en: I'll follow up on this and get back to you.
I follow the news regularly.

tip: "Türk kahvesi" is ordered by sugar level: sade (plain), orta (medium), şekerli (sweet).

examples.tr: Bir Türk kahvesi, orta şekerli lütfen.
examples.en: One Turkish coffee, medium sweet, please.
I can't wake up in the mornings without coffee.
How about a coffee?

examples.tr: Bir fincan kahvenin kırk yıl hatırı vardır.
examples.en: A cup of coffee is remembered for forty years. (Kindness is never forgotten.)

meaning: to take, to get, to buy
tip: Very flexible: "ekmek aldım" (I bought bread), "mesaj aldım" (I got a message).

examples.en: I bought bread from the market.
I want to buy this jacket.

examples.tr: Senden bir mesaj aldım ama açamadım.
examples.en: I got a message from you but couldn't open it.
Don't forget to take your umbrella.

tip: For arranged meetings: "Saat beşte kafede buluşalım."

examples.en: Let's meet at the café at six.
We're meeting up with friends at the weekend.
Where are we meeting?
We haven't been able to meet up for a long time.

tip: "Tercih etmek" = to prefer: "Çayı kahveye tercih ederim."

examples.en: I prefer tea to coffee.
Which one do you prefer?

examples.tr: Pencere kenarını mı tercih edersiniz, koridoru mu?
examples.en: Would you prefer a window seat or an aisle seat?
This is entirely your choice.

tip: "Fişi alabilir miyim?" = Can I have the receipt? Also an electrical plug.

examples.en: Would you like your receipt?
You need a receipt for a return.
Don't forget to unplug the iron.
I keep receipts in a box.

tip: "Hazır mısın?" = Are you ready? "Hazır yemek" = ready meal.

examples.en: Are you ready? We're leaving.
The food is ready, please come to the table.
The documents will be ready tomorrow.
I'm not ready for this yet.

tip: "Ne tavsiye edersiniz?" = What do you recommend? Great for restaurants.

examples.en: What do you recommend?

examples.tr: Bu kitabı sana kesinlikle tavsiye ederim.
examples.en: I definitely recommend this book to you.

examples.tr: Doktor bol su içmemi tavsiye etti.
examples.en: The doctor recommended that I drink plenty of water.

examples.tr: Bana iyi bir restoran tavsiye eder misin?
examples.en: Can you recommend a good restaurant?

tip: The standard reply to "teşekkür ederim". Also used to mean "please, go ahead".

examples.en: "Thanks!" "You're welcome."

examples.tr: Rica ederim, ne demek, her zaman.
examples.en: You're welcome, don't mention it, anytime.
Please, after you.

examples.tr: Sizden bir ricam var: kapıyı kapatır mısınız?
examples.en: I have a favour to ask: could you close the door?

tip: "Anlaştık!" = Deal! "İyi anlaşmak" = to get along well.

examples.en: Okay, deal!
My flatmate and I get along very well.
We couldn't agree on the price.

examples.tr: Saat konusunda anlaşalım, sonra gerisini konuşuruz.
examples.en: Let's agree on the time, then we'll talk about the rest.

tip: From "bilmek". "Bilmem" is a shorter, more casual form.

examples.en: I don't know, we need to ask him.
I don't know the address, can you send it to me?
I don't know what to do.
I don't know, maybe I'll come.

tip: "Değişmek" = to change by itself. "Para değiştirmek" = to exchange money.

examples.en: We had to change our plans.
Can I exchange this shirt?
I forgot to change my password.
This city has changed a lot.

tip: Also a noun: "kalabalık" = crowd.

examples.en: The metro is very crowded in the mornings.
The market gets crowded at the weekend.
I come from a big family.
I lost him in the crowd.

tip: "Acele etme" = take your time. "Acelem var" = I'm in a hurry.

examples.en: Hurry up, the film is starting!
Don't rush, we have time.
Sorry, I'm in a bit of a hurry.
The devil gets into hasty work. (Haste makes waste.)

tip: "Tembellik yapmak" = to be lazy, to slack off.

examples.tr: Bugün çok tembelim, hiçbir şey yapmak istemiyorum.
examples.en: I'm very lazy today, I don't want to do anything.
We had a lazy Sunday.
Don't be lazy, get up and help.

examples.tr: Kedimiz çok tembel, bütün gün uyuyor.
examples.en: Our cat is very lazy, it sleeps all day.

tip: Great for correcting or softening: "Aslında haklısın."

examples.en: Actually, you're right.
Actually, I'm off today.

examples.tr: Aslında çok iyi biri, sadece biraz utangaç.
examples.en: He's actually a very nice person, just a bit shy.
Actually, I don't know what I want.

meaning: to close, to turn off, to hang up
tip: "Telefonu kapatmak" = to hang up or switch off the phone.

examples.en: Close the door on your way out.
Could you turn off the TV?
I'll call you later, I have to hang up now.
The shop closes at nine.

tip: "Önermek" = to suggest.

examples.tr: Bir önerim var: yarın erken başlayalım.
examples.en: I have a suggestion: let's start early tomorrow.
We look forward to your suggestions.
Can you suggest a nice restaurant?
Her suggestion was the most sensible.

tip: "Uyku" is the noun. "İyi uyudun mu?" = Did you sleep well?

examples.en: I slept very well last night.
The baby is sleeping, be quiet.
I usually go to sleep around eleven.
Try to sleep a bit on the journey.

tip: "Emeğine sağlık" = thanks for your hard work (said after someone made something).

examples.en: Thanks for all your hard work, it's turned out great!
I put a lot of work into this.
My mother's efforts can never be repaid.
There's no success without hard work.

tip: "Hedef koymak" = to set a goal.

examples.en: My goal this year is to improve my Turkish.
Focus on your goal.
We reached our sales target.
Setting small goals boosts motivation.

tip: "Spor yapmak" is more common in speech for "to exercise".

examples.tr: Her sabah on dakika egzersiz yapıyorum.
examples.en: I exercise for ten minutes every morning.
The doctor advised me to exercise regularly.
You can do this exercise at home too.

examples.tr: Egzersizden sonra kendimi çok iyi hissediyorum.
examples.en: I feel great after exercising.

tip: "Doktora gitmek" = to go to the doctor.

examples.en: I need to go to the doctor, my throat hurts.
The doctor told me to rest for a few days.

examples.tr: Bu hastanede iyi bir doktor tanıyor musun?
examples.en: Do you know a good doctor at this hospital?
Doctor, I have a fever.

tip: "Bütçeye uygun" = affordable, within budget.

examples.en: We went over our budget this month.
We're looking for an affordable hotel.

examples.tr: Tatil için ne kadar bütçe ayırdın?
examples.en: How much budget did you set aside for the holiday?

examples.tr: Bütçe yapmak para biriktirmeye yardımcı oluyor.
examples.en: Making a budget helps you save money.

tip: "Neden" and "niye" ask "why". "Sebep olmak" = to cause.

examples.en: What's the reason for your being late?
The driver who caused the accident fled.
Everything happens for a reason.
He got angry for no reason.

tip: For exams or interviews people also say "Başarılar!" (wishing success).

examples.en: Good luck in your interview!
Good luck for tomorrow's match.
All the best in the exam, good luck!
Good luck in your new city.

tip: "İzinliyim" = I'm off (work). "Yıllık izin" = annual leave.

examples.en: I'm off tomorrow.
I got a day off from the manager.
I'll use my annual leave in the summer.
With your permission, I'd like to ask something.

tip: "Tebrik ederim" is slightly more formal.

examples.en: Congratulations on your new job!
You passed the exam, congratulations!
Congratulations, it was a great presentation.
Congratulations on your baby.

tip: "Mutluluk" = happiness. "Mutlu yıllar" = Happy new year / happy birthday.

examples.en: I'm very happy to see you.
I'm very happy in my new job.
Happy new year! / Happy birthday!
Little things make me happy.

tip: Intransitive: "Süt bitti" = We're out of milk. Very common at home and in shops.

examples.en: We're out of milk, could you drop by the market?
When does the meeting end?
My phone's battery has died.
The holiday ended so quickly.

tip: Neighbours matter in Turkish culture: "Komşu komşunun külüne muhtaçtır."

examples.en: Our new neighbours are very friendly.
Our neighbour brought us börek.
The neighbour watered our plants while we were on holiday.
Neighbours need each other, even for ashes. (Neighbours always need each other.)

tip: "Yollamak" is a casual synonym.

examples.en: Could you send me the address?
I sent the documents by email.
I sent my mom a parcel.
I sent the message to the wrong person.

tip: Also means "but" at the start of a sentence: "Gelirim, yalnız biraz geç."

examples.en: I live alone.
I need to be alone.
I'll come, but I might be a bit late.
Don't feel alone, we're here.

tip: Very common casual agreement, like "exactly" or "totally".

examples.en: "It was a really tiring day." "Totally."

examples.tr: Aynen öyle, ben de aynı şeyi düşünüyorum.
examples.en: Exactly, I think the same thing.
He told me exactly the same.

examples.tr: Sen nasıl yaptıysan ben de aynen yaptım.
examples.en: I did it exactly the way you did.

tip: Two meanings: the day Sunday and an open-air market. "Pazarlık" = bargaining.

examples.en: What are you doing on Sunday?
We buy fruit and vegetables at the market.
I did a bit of bargaining at the market.
Back to work again on Monday.

tip: "Tokum, teşekkürler" is how to politely refuse more food.

examples.en: Thanks, I'm full.
I'm too full, I can't eat dessert.

examples.tr: Kahvaltıda yumurta yersen öğlene kadar tok kalırsın.
examples.en: If you eat eggs at breakfast you stay full until noon.

examples.tr: Tok karnına alışveriş yapmak daha iyi.
examples.en: It's better to shop on a full stomach.

tip: "Teslim etmek" = to deliver, to hand over. "Teslim tarihi" = deadline.

examples.en: When will the delivery be made?
Is there free delivery?
We delivered the project on time.

examples.tr: Teslim tarihi yarın, acele etmemiz lazım.
examples.en: The deadline is tomorrow, we need to hurry.

tip: "Kaç beden giyiyorsunuz?" = What size do you wear? Sizes: S, M, L are read in English.

examples.tr: Bunun bir büyük bedeni var mı?
examples.en: Do you have this in a larger size?
What size do you wear?

examples.tr: Bu beden bana biraz dar geldi.
examples.en: This size felt a bit tight on me.

examples.tr: Beden sağlığı kadar ruh sağlığı da önemli.
examples.en: Mental health is as important as physical health.

tip: As an answer it means "sure". "Olmaz" means "no way" or "that won't work".

examples.en: "Will you come tomorrow?" "Sure."
Okay, we'll talk in the evening.

examples.tr: Böyle olmaz, başka bir yol bulalım.
examples.en: This won't work, let's find another way.
How can that be?

tip: "Şimdilik" = for now. "Şu an" = right now.

examples.en: I'm not available now.
Everything is fine for now.
We need to leave right now.
Now I understand!

tip: "Alışmak" = to get used to. "Kötü alışkanlık" = bad habit.

examples.tr: Her sabah yürümek iyi bir alışkanlık.
examples.en: Walking every morning is a good habit.
I'm trying to give up my bad habits.

examples.tr: Yeni şehre alışmak biraz zaman aldı.
examples.en: Getting used to the new city took some time.
I made reading a habit.

tip: "Bugünlerde" = these days.

examples.en: The weather is lovely today.
What's the date today?
I'm very busy these days.
I left work early today.

meaning: to read, to study at school
tip: Also means studying a subject: "Üniversitede mühendislik okuyorum."

examples.en: I read a book before going to bed.
I just read your message.
I'm studying computer engineering at university.
Read the contract carefully.

tip: "Saygılı" = respectful. "Saygılarımla" = Kind regards (in emails).

examples.en: You have to show respect to everyone.
We respect our elders.
Kind regards, Ahmet.
It's important to respect different opinions.

tip: Takes the dative: "otobüse binmek", "bisiklete binmek".

examples.en: Which bus do I need to take?
I got on the metro at Taksim.
We ride bikes at the weekends.
I got on a plane for the first time.

tip: "Sorumlu" = responsible. "Sorumluluk almak" = to take responsibility.

examples.en: I'm responsible for this project.
He took responsibility for the mistake.

examples.tr: Çocuk sahibi olmak büyük bir sorumluluk.
examples.en: Having children is a big responsibility.
Who is responsible for this?

tip: "Yıkanmak" = to wash oneself or to be washed.

examples.en: Wash your hands before eating.
I'll wash the dishes.
I had the car washed at the weekend.

examples.tr: Bu kazağı soğuk suda yıkamak lazım.
examples.en: This sweater needs to be washed in cold water.

tip: "Kiralık" = for rent. "Kira" = the rent.

examples.en: We rented a car on holiday.

examples.tr: Merkeze yakın bir daire kiralamak istiyoruz.
examples.en: We want to rent a flat close to the centre.

examples.tr: Bu ev kiralık mı, satılık mı?
examples.en: Is this house for rent or for sale?
How much is it to rent a bike?

tip: "Maaş günü" = payday. "Zam" = pay rise.

examples.en: Salaries are paid on the fifteenth of the month.
I got a pay rise this year.
I'm eagerly waiting for payday.
My salary barely covers the rent.

tip: "Ne anlama geliyor?" = What does it mean? "Anlamlı" = meaningful.

examples.en: What does this word mean?
What do you think is the meaning of life?

examples.tr: Bu hediye benim için çok anlamlı.
examples.en: This gift is very meaningful to me.
Let's not have a pointless argument.

tip: With a verb: "gitmek istiyorum" (I want to go). Also used for ordering: "iki çay istiyoruz".

examples.en: I want a glass of water.
I want to talk to you.
We asked the waiter for the bill.
Let's eat whatever you want.

tip: "seni bekliyorum" = I'm waiting for you. Also "to expect": "Bunu beklemiyordum."

examples.en: I'm waiting for you in front of the door.
We waited twenty minutes for the bus.
I wasn't expecting a result like this.
Could you wait a bit, I'm coming right away.

tip: "Ne zaman?" = When? "Zamanım yok" = I don't have time.

examples.en: When are you coming?
I have no time at all today.
It's lovely spending time with you.
Time passes very quickly.

tip: For living in a city: "İzmir'de yaşıyorum". Also "to go through": "zor bir dönem yaşadım".

examples.en: I've been living in Ankara for five years.

examples.tr: Bu yıl çok güzel şeyler yaşadık.
examples.en: We experienced lots of beautiful things this year.
I live with my family.
I'm trying to live in the moment.

tip: For places: "Otel dolu" = the hotel is fully booked.

examples.en: Unfortunately all the tables are taken.
I filled the glass, now it's full.
My schedule is very full this week.
The bus was very full, I had to stand.

tip: Said both when arriving and when leaving in the evening.

examples.tr: İyi akşamlar, iki kişilik masanız var mı?
examples.en: Good evening, do you have a table for two?
Good evening, see you tomorrow.

examples.tr: Kasadaki çocuk bize iyi akşamlar diledi.
examples.en: The boy at the checkout wished us a good evening.
Good evening, everyone, let's start the meeting.

tip: "Kartla ödemek" = to pay by card. "Nakit" = cash.

examples.en: Can I pay by card?
I'm paying the bill this time.
We pay the rent at the start of every month.
I paid the bill online.

tip: "Elbise" is a dress. "Kıyafet" is clothes in general.

examples.tr: Yarın için ne kıyafet giyeceğime karar veremedim.
examples.en: I couldn't decide what to wear tomorrow.
I put my clothes in the suitcase.
This shop has nice clothes.
I'm going to donate my old clothes.

tip: "Önemli değil" = It's nothing / no problem.

examples.en: This meeting is very important.
I'm going to tell you something important.
Health is more important than anything.
Your opinion matters to me.

tip: "Yoruldum" = I'm tired. "Yorgun" is the adjective.

examples.en: I'm very tired today.
I got tired climbing the stairs.
If you're tired, rest a bit.
He works for hours without getting tired.

tip: "Gidiş-dönüş bilet" = return ticket. "Tek yön" = one way.

examples.en: Two tickets, please.
How much is a return ticket?
I bought the concert tickets online.
I lost my ticket, what should I do?

tip: "Yemek yapmak" is more common in speech for "to cook a meal".

examples.en: I'm cooking pasta tonight.
How do you cook your rice?
Let the meat cook a bit more.
My mom makes the best börek.

tip: "Heyecan" = excitement. "Heyecanlanmak" = to get excited or nervous.

examples.en: I'm very excited about tomorrow's holiday.
The match was very exciting.
I was a bit nervous on my first day at work.
Don't get nervous, everything will go well.

tip: "Hava nasıl?" = What's the weather like? "Hava durumu" = weather forecast.

examples.en: What's the weather like today?

examples.tr: Hava durumuna göre yarın yağmur yağacak.
examples.en: According to the forecast it will rain tomorrow.
I need to get some fresh air.
Let's go home before it gets dark.

tip: "Boş musunuz?" = Are you free? "Boş zaman" = free time.

examples.en: Is this seat free?
The fridge is completely empty, we need to go to the market.
What do you do in your free time?
Forget it, it's not important.

tip: "Belirsiz" = uncertain, unclear.

examples.en: Uncertainty makes me very tense.
The time of the meeting is still unclear.
The uncertainty in the economy continues.
We postponed it indefinitely.

tip: "Tanıştığıma memnun oldum" = Nice to meet you.

examples.en: Nice to meet you.
I met my spouse at university.
Let me introduce you to my friend.
Have we met before?

tip: Describes the relationship between neighbours, a valued tradition in Turkey.

examples.tr: Eskiden komşuluk ilişkileri çok daha güçlüydü.
examples.en: Relationships between neighbours used to be much stronger.

examples.tr: Komşuluk için bir tabak tatlı gönderdik.
examples.en: We sent over a plate of dessert as a neighbourly gesture.
Neighbourliness is still alive in this neighbourhood.
Good neighbourly relations matter more than anything.

tip: "Fırsat bulmak" = to find the chance. "Fırsatı kaçırmak" = to miss the chance.

examples.en: Don't miss this opportunity.
I'll call you when I get the chance.
An opportunity to work abroad came up.
This offer is an opportunity not to be missed.

tip: Don't confuse it with "aç!" meaning "open!" from "açmak". "Açım" = I'm hungry.

examples.en: I'm very hungry, what can we eat?
Don't go shopping on an empty stomach.
I didn't have breakfast, I'm still hungry.
The cat must be hungry, it keeps meowing.

tip: "Üzülmek" = to be upset. "Çok üzüldüm" = I'm so sorry to hear that.

examples.en: Why are you sad?
I'm very sorry to hear that.
I'm a bit sad because we lost the match.
I'm sorry, I can't help.

tip: "Hemen geliyorum" = I'm coming right away.

examples.en: I'm coming right away, one minute.
When I got home I fell asleep right away.
You need to do this right away.
It's almost finished.

tip: "Beklentim yüksekti" = My expectations were high.

examples.en: The film didn't meet my expectations.

examples.tr: Beklentilerini düşük tut, daha az hayal kırıklığı yaşarsın.
examples.en: Keep your expectations low and you'll be less disappointed.
What do you expect from this job?
The result exceeded expectations.

tip: "İki gün önce" = two days ago. "Yemekten önce" = before the meal.

examples.en: I arrived two days ago.
Wash your hands before the meal.

examples.tr: Önce ben gideyim, sonra sen gel.
examples.en: Let me go first, then you come.

examples.tr: Daha önce hiç Türkiye'de bulundun mu?
examples.en: Have you ever been to Turkey before?

meaning: to like (something you see or try)
tip: Used for liking a specific thing, like clothes, food or a post. Takes the accusative.

examples.en: I really like this dress.
Did you like the food?
I liked your photo.

examples.tr: Film fena değildi ama çok beğenmedim.
examples.en: The film wasn't bad but I didn't love it.

tip: "Şaka mı yapıyorsun?" = Are you kidding? "Şaka şaka" = just kidding.

examples.en: Are you kidding me?
I'm joking, don't get angry.
He always jokes around.

examples.tr: Şaka bir yana, bu çok önemli.
examples.en: Joking aside, this is very important.

tip: "Kaybolmak" = to get lost.

examples.en: I lost my wallet.
We lost the match in the last minute.
Let's not waste time.
I got lost in the city, can you help me?

tip: "Beraber" is a common synonym.

examples.en: Let's have dinner together tonight.
We work together.
We're stronger together.
We went on holiday together with friends.

tip: "Saat kaç?" = What time is it? "Saat kaçta?" = At what time?

examples.en: What time is it?
What time does the film start?
I've been waiting for two hours.

examples.tr: Babam bana bir saat hediye etti.
examples.en: My dad gave me a watch as a present.

tip: Softens a statement: "Galiba yağmur yağacak."

examples.en: I think it's going to rain.
I think we got on the wrong bus.
You're probably right.
I think I left my phone at home.

tip: "Toplantıdayım" = I'm in a meeting.

examples.en: I'm in a meeting right now, I'll call later.
The meeting has been postponed to tomorrow.
We discussed the new project in the meeting.
Could you send the link to the online meeting?

tip: "Temiz hava" = fresh air.

examples.en: The room looks spotless, well done.
Is there a clean towel?

examples.tr: Biraz temiz hava almak için dışarı çıktım.
examples.en: I went out to get some fresh air.
This city is very clean.

tip: Very casual greeting between friends. Reply: "İyilik, senden?"

examples.en: Hey, what's up?
"What's up?" "All good, you?"
What's up, how's work going?

examples.tr: Uzun zamandır ses yok, ne haber?
examples.en: Haven't heard from you in ages, what's new?

tip: "Sohbet etmek" = to chat. A central part of Turkish social life.

examples.tr: Dün akşam uzun uzun sohbet ettik.
examples.en: We had a long chat last night.
It's very pleasant to chat with her.

examples.tr: Çay eşliğinde güzel bir sohbet yaptık.
examples.en: We had a nice chat over tea.
Everyone in the group chat is talking about the holiday.

tip: For taking clothes off use "çıkarmak".

examples.en: What should I wear today?
It's cold, put on a coat.
I wore a suit for the meeting.
I've never worn these shoes.

tip: "Tecrübe" is a very common synonym, especially in job contexts.

examples.tr: Bu alanda beş yıllık deneyimim var.
examples.en: I have five years of experience in this field.

examples.tr: Yurt dışında yaşamak harika bir deneyimdi.
examples.en: Living abroad was a wonderful experience.
We're looking for someone experienced.
Everything gets easier with experience.

tip: "Nöbetçi eczane" = the pharmacy on night or weekend duty.

examples.en: Where is the nearest pharmacy?
Which pharmacy is on duty?

examples.tr: Eczaneden baş ağrısı için ilaç aldım.
examples.en: I got medicine for a headache from the pharmacy.
The pharmacist recommended this cream.

tip: "Ne ilginç!" = How interesting!

examples.en: What an interesting story!
I find this topic very interesting.
There were interesting pieces at the museum.
Interesting, I had never thought of that.

tip: Past tense of "anlamak". "Anlamadım" (I didn't understand) is just as useful.

examples.en: Okay, got it, thanks.
I didn't understand, can you say it again?
Now I understand what you mean.

examples.tr: Anladım ki bu iş kolay değil.
examples.en: I realised this job isn't easy.

tip: "Fotoğraf çekmek" = to take a photo.

examples.en: Could you take a photo of us?
Have you seen the holiday photos?
Taking photos is forbidden here.
You look great in this photo.

tip: "Keyfin nasıl?" = How are you doing? "Keyif almak" = to enjoy.

examples.en: How are you feeling today?

examples.tr: Bu kitabı okumaktan çok keyif aldım.
examples.en: I really enjoyed reading this book.
Drinking tea on the balcony is a real pleasure.
I'm not in the mood, I'll stay home.

tip: "İçgüdü" = instinct. "İçimden bir ses" = a voice inside me (a gut feeling).

examples.en: I trust my intuition.

examples.tr: İçimden bir ses bunun doğru olmadığını söylüyor.
examples.en: Something tells me this isn't right.
Your intuitions usually turn out to be right.
I made the decision based on my intuition.

tip: For "there isn't" use "yok"; for "it's not" use "değil". "Hayır" is the direct answer "no".

examples.en: No thanks, I'm full.
No, that's not mine.
"Do you want sugar?" "No."
No, I can't come today.

tip: For small corner shops people also say "bakkal".

examples.tr: Markete gidiyorum, bir şey lazım mı?
examples.en: I'm going to the shop, do you need anything?

examples.tr: Köşedeki market gece yarısına kadar açık.
examples.en: The shop on the corner is open until midnight.
We do the grocery shopping once a week.
Could you get a loaf of bread from the corner shop?

tip: Informal. Use "kusura bakmayın" with strangers or elders.

examples.en: Sorry, I'm late.
I'm sorry, I didn't mean to keep you waiting.
Sorry, I forgot to call yesterday.

examples.tr: Kusura bakma ama bu konuda sana katılmıyorum.
examples.en: Sorry, but I don't agree with you on this.

tip: "Bozuk para" = coins or small change. "Para üstü" = change back.

examples.en: I don't have any money on me.
You forgot your change.
Do you have any change?
I'm saving money for a holiday.

tip: "Sorun değil" = No problem. "Sorun ne?" = What's the problem?

examples.en: No problem, we'll sort it out.
I think there's a problem with the car.
What's the problem, can you tell me?
Let's solve this problem together.

tip: Also a noun: "hasta" = patient. "Hastalanmak" = to get sick.

examples.en: I'm sick today, I won't be able to go to work.
The child is ill, we're taking him to the doctor.
I often get sick in winter.
The doctor examined the patient.

tip: Means both working and studying: "sınava çalışmak" = to study for an exam.

examples.en: I work at a software company.
I need to study for tomorrow's exam.
This machine isn't working.
I'm working from home today.

tip: Also "on purpose" in some contexts: "Özellikle senin için aldım."

examples.en: I love Turkish cuisine, especially breakfast.
I bought this especially for you.

examples.tr: Özellikle hafta sonları trafik çok yoğun.
examples.en: Traffic is very heavy, especially at the weekend.

examples.tr: Özellikle belirtmek istediğim bir şey var.
examples.en: There's something I'd especially like to point out.

tip: "Soda" = sparkling water. "Maden suyu" = mineral water.

examples.en: Can I get a bottle of water?
Is the tap water drinkable?
The hot water isn't coming again.
I try to drink plenty of water every day.

tip: Also "the key to" something: "başarının anahtarı".

examples.en: Where did I put my keys?
I left the key with the building manager.
Do you have the car key?
Working regularly is the key to success.

tip: "Tekrar eder misiniz?" = Could you repeat that?

examples.en: Could you repeat that, please?
I'm glad to see you again.
I review the words every day.
It won't happen again, I promise.

tip: "Annemler" = my mom and family (my parents' home).

examples.en: My mom cooks really well.
I'm going to my parents' place at the weekend.
Happy Mother's Day!
Say hello to your mom and dad.

tip: "Çok kibarsınız" = You're very kind.

examples.en: You're very kind, thank you.
The waiter was very polite and helpful.

examples.tr: Kibar bir dille konuşmak her zaman işe yarar.
examples.en: Speaking politely always works.
Be polite, say thank you to the lady.

tip: "Fiyatı ne kadar?" = How much is it? Also "kaç para?".

examples.en: What's the price of this?
Prices are going up every month.
Can you lower the price a bit?
It's very good value for money.

tip: "Müsait misin?" = Are you free? Also used when getting off a minibus: "Müsait bir yerde!"

examples.en: Are you free tomorrow afternoon?

examples.tr: Şu an müsait değilim, sonra ararım.
examples.en: I'm not available right now, I'll call later.
Can I get off wherever is convenient?
Let me know when you're free.

tip: "Teşekkürler" is shorter and a bit more casual; "sağ ol" is very casual.

examples.en: Thank you very much for your help.
Thank you, you're very kind.

examples.tr: Hediyen için teşekkür ederim, çok beğendim.
examples.en: Thank you for your gift, I really liked it.
"Do you want some water?" "No, thank you."

tip: Takes the accusative: "seni anlıyorum". "Anlamadım" is extremely useful when learning.

examples.en: I understand you very well.
I didn't understand, could you repeat that?

examples.tr: Türkçe filmleri artık daha iyi anlıyorum.
examples.en: I understand Turkish films better now.
I finally understood what you meant.

tip: "Görüşmek" = to meet up, to see each other.

examples.en: I saw you on the metro yesterday.
I can't see well without my glasses.
I've seen this film before.
You see, everything's fine.

tip: "Yetenekli" = talented.

examples.en: She has a real talent for music.
He's a very talented cook.
Everyone has different talents.
Don't waste your talent.

tip: "Konu dışı" = off-topic. "Bu konuda" = on this matter.

examples.en: Our topic today is environmental pollution.
What do you think about this?
Don't change the subject!
We need to talk about an important matter.

tip: Used by everyone, religious or not, to mean "hopefully".

examples.en: Hopefully the weather will be nice tomorrow.
Hopefully you'll pass the exam.
"See you!" "Hopefully."
Hopefully everything goes well.

tip: "Wi-fi şifresi ne?" = What's the Wi-Fi password? Essential in every café.

examples.en: What's the Wi-Fi password?
I forgot my password.
Please enter your card PIN.
It's important to choose a strong password.

tip: For restaurants and online shopping. "Sipariş" = an order.

examples.en: Shall we order food?

examples.tr: İnternetten yeni bir ayakkabı sipariş verdim.
examples.en: I ordered new shoes online.
Are you ready to order?
My order still hasn't arrived.

tip: Usually goes at the end of the request: "Bir çay, lütfen."

examples.en: A tea, please.

examples.tr: Lütfen biraz daha yavaş konuşur musunuz?
examples.en: Could you please speak a bit more slowly?
Please don't forget to close the door.
Can we have the bill, please?

tip: "Güvenli" = safe. "Güvenlik görevlisi" = security guard.

examples.en: For your safety, please fasten your seatbelts.
We need to go through the security check.
Is this place safe at night?
I asked the security guard.

tip: "Hafta sonları" = at weekends. "Hafta içi" = weekdays.

examples.en: What are you doing at the weekend?
I'm very busy on weekdays.
I get up late at weekends.

examples.tr: Bu hafta sonu şehir dışına çıkıyoruz.
examples.en: We're going out of town this weekend.

tip: "Otobüs durağı" = bus stop. In Istanbul you pay with an "İstanbulkart".

examples.en: Where is the bus stop?
Does this bus go to Kadıköy?
What time is the last bus?
I couldn't find a seat on the bus.

tip: Tea is served in small tulip glasses. "Açık" = weak, "demli" = strong.

examples.en: Would you like a tea?
I like my tea weak.
The tea has brewed, come on.

examples.tr: İş yerinde günde beş bardak çay içiyorum.
examples.en: I drink five glasses of tea a day at work.

tip: Takes the dative: "odaya girmek", "sınava girmek" (to take an exam).

examples.en: May I come in?
I'm taking an important exam tomorrow.
Please don't come in with your shoes on.
I entered the password wrong.

tip: Note the long â. Don't confuse it with "hala" (paternal aunt).

examples.en: Are you still sleeping?
My order still hasn't arrived.

examples.tr: Yıllar geçti ama hâlâ aynı yerde oturuyor.
examples.en: Years have passed but she still lives in the same place.
I'm still hungry.

tip: Synonym: "tekrar". "Yine de" = still, nevertheless.

examples.en: Are you late again?
Let's meet again.
I was tired but I came anyway.
Apparently it's going to rain again tomorrow.

tip: Takes the accusative: "müzik dinlemek", "beni dinle". Also "dinlenmek" = to rest.

examples.en: Listen to me, it's very important.
I listen to podcasts on the way.
Which song are you listening to the most?
I listened carefully to what the doctor said.

tip: "Üşümek" = to feel cold: "Üşüyorum".

examples.en: It's very cold outside, wear a coat.
I want to drink something cold.
The soup has gone cold, shall I heat it up?
She was a bit cold towards me.

tip: Transitive: you finish something. "Bitmek" is when something itself ends or runs out.

examples.en: I've finished my homework.

examples.tr: Bu işi cumaya kadar bitirmemiz lazım.
examples.en: We need to finish this job by Friday.
Finish your food, then we'll go out.
I finished the book in two days.

tip: Directions: "sağda" = on the right. Also "alive": "sağ salim" = safe and sound.

examples.en: The pharmacy is on the right, next to the bank.
Turn right at the lights.
I write with my right hand.
We got home safe and sound.

tip: Stronger and more sincere than "pardon". Takes the ablative: "senden özür dilerim".

examples.en: I'm sorry, I misunderstood.
I apologize to you, you were right.

examples.tr: Geç cevap verdiğim için özür dilerim.
examples.en: I'm sorry for replying late.
We apologize for our mistake.

tip: For weather: "Hava çok sıcak". Also warm in personality: "sıcak biri".

examples.en: The weather is very hot today.
A hot tea would do you good.
Careful, the plate is hot.
His family welcomed us very warmly.

tip: "İş-yaşam dengesi" = work-life balance.

examples.tr: İş ve özel hayat arasında denge kurmak zor.
examples.en: It's hard to balance work and private life.
I lost my balance and fell.
I pay attention to eating a balanced diet.
In life, balance in everything matters.

tip: "Mahalle" is the local community; "mahalleli" means the locals.

examples.en: Which neighbourhood do you live in?
There's a market in our neighbourhood every Tuesday.

examples.tr: Bu mahalle çok sakin ve güvenli.
examples.en: This neighbourhood is very quiet and safe.
The bread from the bakery in our neighbourhood is delicious.

tip: Used to ask someone to wait. "Bir saniye" works the same way.

examples.en: One minute, I'm coming right away.
Could you wait a moment?
Wait a minute, this isn't right.
Do you have a minute? Let's talk.

tip: "Baş ağrısı" = headache. "Ağrımak" = to hurt: "Başım ağrıyor".

examples.en: I have a bad headache.
My back pain won't go away.
Do you have a painkiller?
I couldn't sleep because of a toothache.

tip: Don't confuse with "dinlemek" (to listen).

examples.en: I just want to rest at the weekend.
Let's rest a little, then continue.
The doctor told me to rest for a few days.
I rested properly on holiday.

tip: The reply is always "hoş bulduk". Use "hoş geldiniz" for more than one person or politely.

examples.en: Welcome, come in!
"Welcome!" "Glad to be here."
Welcome to our team.
Welcome back from your holiday, how did it go?

tip: "Sanki yıllardır tanışıyoruz" = It's as if we've known each other for years.

examples.en: It's as if we've known each other for years.
It looks as if it's going to rain.

examples.tr: Sanki hiçbir şey olmamış gibi davrandı.
examples.en: He acted as if nothing had happened.
It's as if he doesn't hear me.

tip: "Sabırlı" = patient. "Sabrın sonu selamettir" = patience brings good results.

examples.en: A bit of patience, it's almost done.
I've run out of patience.
Working with children needs a lot of patience.
Patience leads to salvation. (Good things come to those who wait.)

tip: "biriyle konuşmak" = to talk with someone. "Türkçe konuşmak" = to speak Turkish.

examples.en: Can you speak Turkish?
Let's talk about this tomorrow.
I was talking to my mom on the phone.
Please speak more slowly.

tip: As an adverb: "hızlı konuşmak" = to speak fast.

examples.en: You're speaking too fast, I don't understand.
Which is the fastest way?
The internet here is very fast.
Time is passing so fast.

tip: "Yanlış anlamak" = to misunderstand.

examples.en: I must have called the wrong number.
Don't get me wrong.
I got on the wrong bus.
There's a mistake in this sentence.

tip: Directions: "sağa dön" (turn right), "sola dön" (turn left).

examples.en: Turn right at the second street.
What time are you coming back home?
I've just come back from holiday.

examples.tr: Bir dakika, telefonumu almak için geri dönüyorum.
examples.en: One minute, I'm going back to get my phone.

tip: "Fark etmez" = It doesn't matter. "Fark etmek" = to notice.

examples.en: What's the difference between the two?
It doesn't matter, whichever.
I noticed you got a haircut.

examples.tr: Küçük bir değişiklik büyük fark yaratır.
examples.en: A small change makes a big difference.

tip: "Gerçekten mi?" = Really?

examples.en: Really? I can't believe it!
This food is really delicious.
I'm really grateful for your help.
Do you really want to go?

tip: Only for saying goodbye at night or before sleeping, never as a greeting.

examples.en: Good night, I'm getting up early tomorrow.

examples.tr: Çocuklara iyi geceler deyip ışığı kapattım.
examples.en: I said good night to the kids and turned off the light.

examples.tr: Mesajına geç cevap verdim, iyi geceler.
examples.en: I replied to your message late, good night.
Good night, sweet dreams!

tip: Takes the dative: "şakaya gülmek". "Gülümsemek" = to smile.

examples.en: I laughed a lot at this joke.
Why are you laughing?

examples.tr: Film o kadar komikti ki gülmekten ağladık.
examples.en: The film was so funny we cried laughing.
Everyone is smiling in the photo.

tip: "Durum ne?" = What's the situation? "Bu durumda" = in this case.

examples.tr: Durum nedir, her şey yolunda mı?
examples.en: What's the situation, is everything okay?
What should we do in this case?
The patient's condition is improving.
The economic situation affects everyone.

tip: Takes the dative: "bana bak". Also "to take care of": "çocuğa bakmak".

examples.en: Look at that, how lovely!
Excuse me, could you help me? (to a waiter or shop assistant)
I'm looking after my nephew this weekend.
Let me check online right away.

tip: "Yetenek" = talent. "Beceri" is a skill you develop.

examples.en: I want to improve my communication skills.
Cooking is a skill too.

examples.tr: Bu iş için hangi beceriler gerekiyor?
examples.en: What skills are needed for this job?
His manual skills are very good.

tip: "İş görüşmesi" is a common synonym.

examples.en: I have an important interview tomorrow.
How did the interview go?
I worked hard to prepare for the interview.
They asked me about my experience in the interview.

tip: Opposite: "tembel" (lazy).

examples.en: My sibling is a very hardworking student.
Hardworking people win in the end.
The new intern is very hardworking.

examples.tr: Çalışkan olmak yetmez, akıllı da çalışmak lazım.
examples.en: Being hardworking isn't enough, you also need to work smart.

tip: For "can do": "yüzmeyi biliyorum" (I know how to swim). "Bilmiyorum" = I don't know.

examples.en: Do you know his number?
I know a little Turkish.
I don't know how to drive.
If I had known, I would have told you.

meaning: well done (to someone who cooked or made something)
tip: Say it to whoever cooked your meal. Also for any handmade work.

examples.en: The food is amazing, thank you for cooking!
Thank you mum, it was delicious.

examples.tr: Tabloyu sen mi yaptın? Eline sağlık.
examples.en: Did you paint this? Great work.
Thanks for making the tea.

tip: "Sıra sende" = It's your turn. "Sıraya girmek" = to queue.

examples.en: Whose turn is it?
It's your turn, roll the dice.
There was a long queue at the bank.
Please get in line.

tip: "Cüzdanımı unuttum" is a useful (if unfortunate) sentence.

examples.en: I seem to have left my wallet at home.
Do you have cash in your wallet?
My wallet was stolen on the metro.
I bought a new leather wallet.

tip: "Dün akşam" = last night. "Evvelsi gün" = the day before yesterday.

examples.tr: Dün akşam güzel bir film izledim.
examples.en: I watched a good film last night.
Where were you yesterday?
I sent the parcel yesterday.
I remember it as if it were yesterday.

tip: "Endişe" = worry, anxiety. "Endişelenme" = don't worry.

examples.en: Don't worry, we'll make it on time.
I'm very worried about the exam.
I got worried about you when you didn't call.
There's nothing to worry about.

tip: Said before or after eating. The reply after a meal is often "teşekkürler" or "eline sağlık".

examples.en: The food is here, enjoy your meal!
The waiter put down the plates and said "enjoy".
Enjoy! Did you like it?
Breakfast is ready, enjoy.

tip: "Elektrik faturası" = electricity bill. "Faturalı hat" = contract phone line.

examples.tr: Bu ay elektrik faturası çok yüksek geldi.
examples.en: The electricity bill came very high this month.
I set the bills up on automatic payment.
Could you issue an invoice?
I forgot to pay the water bill.

tip: Takes the dative: "eve yakın" = close to home. Also "yakın arkadaş" = close friend.

examples.en: Where is the nearest pharmacy to here?
The house is very close to my work.
She is my closest friend.
See you soon.

tip: "Çok pahalı" is useful for bargaining at markets.

examples.en: This bag is very expensive.
Rents in Istanbul have become very expensive.

examples.tr: Biraz pahalı ama kalitesi çok iyi.
examples.en: It's a bit expensive but the quality is very good.

examples.tr: Daha az pahalı bir şey var mı?
examples.en: Is there something less expensive?

tip: "Yağmur yağıyor" = It's raining.

examples.en: It's raining outside, take an umbrella.

examples.tr: Yağmurdan sonra hava çok temiz oluyor.
examples.en: The air gets very clean after rain.
We got caught in the rain and got soaked.
It's raining all the time this week.

tip: "İstikrarlı" = stable, consistent.

examples.en: The secret of success is consistency.
I'm looking for a stable job.

examples.tr: Her gün biraz çalışmak istikrar sağlar.
examples.en: Studying a little every day builds consistency.
Prices are expected to stabilise.

tip: "Görevli" = official, attendant.

examples.tr: Bu görevi cumaya kadar bitirmem lazım.
examples.en: I need to finish this task by Friday.
The attendant directed me to the right gate.
Everyone in the team has a role.
Good luck in your new role!

tip: The person asked takes the dative: "öğretmene sordum".

examples.en: Can I ask you something?
We asked a police officer the way.
I asked the price, it turned out to be very expensive.
If you don't know, don't hesitate to ask.

tip: Very casual. "Sağ olun" is the polite or plural form.

examples.tr: Sağ ol kanka, çok yardımcı oldun.
examples.en: Thanks mate, you really helped.
"I held the door." "Thanks."
Thank you, you're very kind.
Thanks for the gift.

tip: "Güvenmek" = to trust. "Kendine güven" = self-confidence.

examples.en: I trust you.
Trust isn't easily earned.
Your self-confidence has grown.
Do you know a reliable repairman?

tip: "Doğum gününü kutlarım" = Happy birthday (lit. I celebrate your birthday).

examples.en: Happy birthday!
We celebrated the new year with my family.
Let's go out for dinner to celebrate your success.
Congratulations on your new job, I'm so happy for you.

tip: "Ailece" = as a family.

examples.en: I spent the weekend with my family.
We have a big family.
Do you miss your family a lot?

examples.tr: Bayramda bütün aile bir araya geldi.
examples.en: The whole family got together for the holiday.

meaning: to join, to attend / to agree
tip: Takes the dative: "toplantıya katılmak" (attend), "sana katılıyorum" (I agree with you).

examples.en: I completely agree with you.
Will you attend tomorrow's meeting?
I don't agree with this idea.
I took part in a marathon for the first time.

tip: "Soru sormak" = to ask a question.

examples.en: I have a question.
Does anyone have a question?
That's a very good question.
I couldn't do three questions in the exam.

tip: Two daily meanings: searching and phoning. "Seni ararım" = I'll call you.

examples.en: I'll call you in the evening.
I'm looking for my glasses, have you seen them?
I'm looking for a new job.
My mom called, she was worried about me.

tip: For people's age use "yaşlı". "Eski" is for objects or former things: "eski arkadaşım".

examples.en: This building is very old.
I gave my old phone to my sibling.
I ran into an old friend yesterday.
My old job was closer.

tip: "Misafirperver" = hospitable. Turks take hospitality seriously.

examples.en: We have guests this evening.
We laid the table for the guests.
Turks are very hospitable.
Please, you're our guest.

meaning: to wonder, to be curious, to worry
tip: "Merak etme" = don't worry. "Merak ediyorum" = I'm curious / I wonder.

examples.en: Don't worry, everything's fine.
I'm really curious what will happen.
My mom was worried about me and called.

examples.tr: Merak ettiğin bir şey var mı?
examples.en: Is there anything you're curious about?

tip: "Çok fazla" = far too much. "Fazla mesai" = overtime.

examples.tr: Bu ceket bana biraz fazla büyük.
examples.en: This jacket is a bit too big for me.
I don't have much time, tell me quickly.
I did overtime this month.

examples.tr: Fazla yemek yedim, şimdi çok tokum.
examples.en: I ate too much, now I'm very full.
