tip: "Hesap lütfen" = The bill, please. Also a bank account or an online account.

examples.en: Can we have the bill?
The bill's on me.
I opened a new account at the bank.
I forgot my account password.

tip: "Kaçıncı kat?" = Which floor? "Zemin kat" = ground floor.

examples.en: Which floor do you live on?
Our office is on the fifth floor.
Take the lift up to the third floor.
The toilets are on the ground floor.

tip: Use it to change the subject or wrap something up.

examples.en: Anyway, we'll talk later.
Luckily the rain stopped.
Anyway, it doesn't matter.

examples.tr: Uçağı kaçırdık, neyse ki bir sonraki bir saat sonra.
examples.en: We missed the plane, luckily the next one is an hour later.

tip: "yürüyüş yapmak" = to go for a walk.

examples.en: I walk to work.
In the evening we walked by the seaside a bit.
How long does it take to walk there?

examples.tr: Günde on bin adım yürümeye çalışıyorum.
examples.en: I try to walk ten thousand steps a day.

tip: "Sessiz ol" = be quiet. Opposite: "gürültülü" (noisy).

examples.en: It's very quiet and peaceful here.
Be quiet, the baby is sleeping.
I put my phone on silent.
Do you know a quiet café?

tip: "Rahat ol" = relax. "Rahatına bak" = make yourself comfortable.

examples.en: These shoes are very comfortable.
Relax, make yourself at home.

examples.tr: Sınavdan sonra rahat bir nefes aldım.
examples.en: I breathed a sigh of relief after the exam.
We had a relaxing weekend.

tip: The most useful intensifier. "Çok teşekkürler" = Thanks a lot.

examples.en: Thank you very much.

examples.tr: Bu şehirde çok güzel yerler var.
examples.en: There are many beautiful places in this city.
I missed you a lot.
Don't put too much sugar in.

tip: "Tarif" alone also means directions: "Yolu tarif eder misiniz?"

examples.en: Could you give me the recipe for this dish?

examples.tr: İnternette güzel bir yemek tarifi buldum.
examples.en: I found a nice recipe online.
I cook with my mom's recipes.
Could you give me directions?

tip: "Dikkat!" = Caution! "Dikkat etmek" = to pay attention.

examples.en: Caution, there's a step!
Focus your attention in class.
Take care of your health.
Something caught my attention.

tip: Used both for sharing things and posting online.

examples.en: Shall we share the pizza?
I shared the photos in the group.
I share a room with my sibling.
Would you share your idea with us?

tip: "İletişim bilgileri" = contact details. "İletişime geçmek" = to get in touch.

examples.en: Can I get your contact details?
Communication within the team is very important.

examples.tr: Sizinle en kısa sürede iletişime geçeceğiz.
examples.en: We'll get in touch with you as soon as possible.

examples.tr: İyi bir ilişkinin temeli açık iletişimdir.
examples.en: The foundation of a good relationship is open communication.

tip: For waking someone else up use "uyandırmak".

examples.en: I woke up at six this morning.
I woke up before the alarm went off.
Could you wake me up at seven?
I like waking up late at the weekend.

tip: Used until about noon. After that switch to "iyi günler".

examples.en: Good morning! Breakfast is ready.
Good morning, how are you today?
I said good morning to my neighbour and left for work.

examples.tr: Grup sohbetine her sabah biri "günaydın" yazıyor.
examples.en: Every morning someone writes "good morning" in the group chat.

tip: "Yaklaşmak" = to approach, to get close.

examples.tr: Bu soruna farklı bir yaklaşım denemeliyiz.
examples.en: We should try a different approach to this problem.
The teacher's approach to students is very positive.
The exam is approaching, start studying.
His calm approach put everyone at ease.

meaning: to go out, to leave, to exit
tip: Takes the ablative for leaving: "evden çıkmak". "Dışarı çıkmak" = to go out.

examples.en: I left home at eight.
Shall we go out tonight?
I went up the stairs.
When is the new phone coming out?

tip: Works in any situation, formal or casual. "Selam" is the more casual version.

examples.tr: Merhaba, ben Miqdam. Tanıştığıma memnun oldum.
examples.en: Hello, I'm Miqdam. Nice to meet you.
Hi, can I get a tea?

examples.tr: Sabah ofise girince herkese merhaba dedim.
examples.en: When I walked into the office this morning, I said hello to everyone.
Say hello to your mother for me.

tip: "Seni özledim" = I missed you. Very common and warm.

examples.en: I missed you so much.
I miss my mom's cooking.
I miss the sea, let's go to the coast.
Did you miss me?

tip: "Erkenden" = early on.

examples.en: I need to get up early tomorrow.
I arrived early for the meeting.
It's still too early to decide.
Winter came early this year.

tip: "Babaanne" = paternal grandmother. "Anneanne" = maternal grandmother.

examples.en: My father is a retired teacher.
My dad and I go fishing every Sunday.

examples.tr: Babaannem bize çok güzel masallar anlatırdı.
examples.en: My grandmother used to tell us lovely stories.

examples.tr: Babası gibi o da çok çalışkan.
examples.en: Like his father, he is very hardworking.

tip: The reply is "sen de gör" - "may you see it too".

examples.en: "Achoo!" "Bless you!"
"Bless you." "You too."

examples.tr: Arka arkaya hapşırınca herkes "çok yaşa" dedi.
examples.en: When I sneezed again and again, everyone said "bless you".
Bless you, have you caught a cold?

tip: Also "cuisine": "Türk mutfağı" = Turkish cuisine.

examples.en: My mom is cooking in the kitchen.

examples.tr: Türk mutfağı dünyanın en zengin mutfaklarından biri.
examples.en: Turkish cuisine is one of the richest in the world.
Will you help me tidy the kitchen?
The new house's kitchen is very spacious.

tip: "Bana yaz" = text me / write to me.

examples.en: Please write your name here.
Text me when you're free.

examples.tr: Her gün günlüğüme bir şeyler yazıyorum.
examples.en: I write something in my diary every day.
I finished writing the report.

tip: "Mümkünse" = if possible. "Mümkün değil" = impossible.

examples.en: Could you come tomorrow if possible?

examples.tr: Bu işi bir günde bitirmek mümkün değil.
examples.en: It's not possible to finish this job in a day.

examples.tr: Mümkün olan en kısa sürede dönüş yapacağım.
examples.en: I'll get back to you as soon as possible.
Anything is possible.

tip: Also "to find out": "Sonucu yarın öğreneceğiz."

examples.en: I'm learning Turkish.
I learned to swim when I was little.
We'll find out the exam results tomorrow.

examples.tr: Her gün yeni bir kelime öğrenmek istiyorum.
examples.en: I want to learn a new word every day.

tip: Polite way to give bad news, common in shops and offices.

examples.en: Unfortunately this product is out of stock.
Unfortunately I can't come today.
Unfortunately your flight has been cancelled.
Unfortunately what you said is true.

tip: "Tam zamanında" = just in time. "Tam gün" = full-time.

examples.en: You came just in time!
Let's meet at exactly five.
What exactly do you mean?
I work full-time.

tip: The thing said takes the accusative, the listener the dative: "ona gerçeği söyledim".

examples.en: Tell me the truth.
I couldn't hear what you said.
I told him I would come tomorrow.
Let's all sing this song together.

tip: "Planın var mı?" = Do you have plans?

examples.tr: Bu akşam bir planın var mı?
examples.en: Do you have any plans tonight?
Plans have changed, we're going tomorrow.
Everything is going according to plan.

examples.tr: Hafta sonu için bir plan yapalım.
examples.en: Let's make a plan for the weekend.

tip: "İlaç almak/içmek" = to take medicine.

examples.tr: Bu ilacı günde iki kez içmelisin.
examples.en: You should take this medicine twice a day.
Can I buy medicine without a prescription?
Did you take your medicine?
Laughter is the best medicine.

tip: Also for devices and calls: "ışığı aç" (turn on the light), "telefonu aç" (answer the phone).

examples.en: Could you open the window? It's very hot.
Could you turn on the light?
I called but he didn't answer the phone.
I opened a new account at the bank.

tip: "Randevu almak" = to make an appointment.

examples.en: I need to make an appointment with the doctor.
I have an appointment at three.
I want to cancel my appointment.
I booked an appointment at the hairdresser for tomorrow.

tip: "Başvurmak" = to apply: "İşe başvurdum."

examples.en: I sent my application yesterday.

examples.tr: Başvuru için son tarih ne zaman?
examples.en: When is the deadline for applications?
I applied for jobs at three companies.
Your application is being reviewed.

tip: Also means "to reside": "Kadıköy'de oturuyorum" = I live in Kadıköy.

examples.en: Please, have a seat.
I live in Kadıköy.
I sat at the computer all day.
Let's sit down and rest a bit.

tip: Takes the dative: "gitmeye karar verdim" = I decided to go.

examples.en: I haven't decided yet.
We've decided to move.
I can't decide which one to buy.
Think carefully before you decide.

tip: "Tasarruf etmek" = to save (money, energy, time).

examples.tr: Elektrikten tasarruf etmek için ışıkları kapatıyorum.
examples.en: I turn off the lights to save electricity.
We should save a bit this month.

examples.tr: Toplu taşıma kullanarak çok tasarruf ediyorum.
examples.en: I save a lot by using public transport.

examples.tr: Zamandan tasarruf etmek için yemeği önceden hazırlıyorum.
examples.en: I prepare meals in advance to save time.

tip: Takes the dative (-e/-a): eve gitmek, okula gitmek. The t becomes d before a vowel: gidiyorum.

examples.en: I'm going to Istanbul tomorrow.
I go to work by bus every morning.
Shall we go to the cinema at the weekend?

examples.tr: Çok geç oldu, artık gitmem lazım.
examples.en: It's got very late, I need to go now.

tip: "Mesaj atmak" = to text, to send a message.

examples.en: I sent you a message, did you see it?
Text me when you're free.

examples.tr: Mesajına geç cevap verdiğim için kusura bakma.
examples.en: Sorry for replying late to your message.
I left a voice message.

tip: "Dikkat et!" = Be careful! "Dikkatli ol" = take care.

examples.en: Be careful on the road.
We need to be very careful about this.
He is a careful driver.
Watch out, the floor is slippery!

meaning: to be, to become, to happen
tip: Used for becoming and happening: "Ne oldu?" (What happened?), "doktor olmak" (to become a doctor).

examples.en: What happened? Why are you sad?
When I grow up I want to become a doctor.
I'll be at home tomorrow.

examples.tr: Bu iş olmaz, başka bir plan yapalım.
examples.en: This won't work, let's make another plan.

tip: "Yarın sabah" = tomorrow morning. "Öbür gün" = the day after tomorrow.

examples.en: See you tomorrow.
I'll leave early tomorrow morning.
Let's leave this until tomorrow.
We're going on holiday the day after tomorrow.

tip: With a negative verb: "henüz bitmedi" = not finished yet.

examples.en: I haven't decided yet.
The film hasn't started yet.
He's only twenty.
I've just arrived, let me catch my breath.

tip: Synonym: "yalnızca".

examples.en: I only want a tea.
I'm just looking, thanks.
It only takes five minutes.
I just wanted to talk to you.

tip: A warm way to end a conversation or message.

examples.en: Bye, take care of yourself.
If you're sick, rest and take care of yourself.

examples.tr: Yolun açık olsun, kendine iyi bak!
examples.en: Have a safe trip, take care!

examples.tr: Annem her telefonda "kendine iyi bak" der.
examples.en: My mom says "take care of yourself" on every call.
